description: utopia-php/audit: audit logs through Audit, stored by the Database adapter (a utopia-php/database collection, on MariaDB, SQLite or Memory) or the ClickHouse adapter (a MergeTree table over ClickHouse's HTTP interface, on a local ClickHouse or a recording client); Log and the lenient Query factories.

scrub.reason: logs carry the time they were written ($createdAt, $updatedAt and a default time), which differs between runs and runtimes
Database ids are ID::unique() and ClickHouse ids uniqid('', true), both made from the clock

clickhouse.new.doc: new ClickHouse(host, username, password, port, secure, client) as a handle: on service `audit-clickhouse` (host, port and credentials from its URL, then setDatabase(${ns})) unless `host` is given; over the test suite's recording client (`Tests\Adapter\Client`) with `fake`

database.new.doc: new Adapter\Database(new Database(<engine>, new Cache(new None()))) as a handle, the database `database` (${ns}) with namespace `namespace` (`namespace`), created unless it exists (DatabaseTest::initializeAudit); engine mariadb (service database-mariadb), sqlite (a file under /tmp/compat-fs/${ns}/) or memory

clickhouse.call.doc: One adapter.<method> call (args as that operation's) on a fresh new ClickHouse('clickhouse', 'user', 'secret', 8124) over the recording client, after the `config` setters (set_namespace, set_tenant, ...: value) and with `responses` queued ({status, body} or {fail: message}, a ConnectionException): {result, error: {class, message} | null, requests} (requests as fake.requests reports them)

quirks.description: With shared tables and a tenant, the DELETE carries the tenant filter as a typed parameter ({param0:UInt64}) but cleanup() sends only its own `datetime` parameter, never the builder's bindings: ClickHouse rejects the statement, so cleanup() fails with shared tables.
quirks.case: ClickHouseSqlSnapshotTest.json#cleanup with shared tables binds no tenant parameter (quirk)

quirks.description: Every request names the adapter's database (X-ClickHouse-Database), the CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS of setup() too: ClickHouse refuses it with UNKNOWN_DATABASE, so setup() only works on a database that exists already.
quirks.case: ClickHouse.json#setup on a database that does not exist (quirk)

quirks.description: On SQLite, Database::exists() of the database is false even after create(), so setup() refuses with `You need to create the database before running Audit setup`.
quirks.case: Database.json#setup on SQLite: its exists() finds no database, so setup refuses

bound.clickhouse_count: A ClickHouse round trip (the server scans the table), the same on both runtimes, dominates the call

deviations.php: An array (or object) as the value of a date column (a `time` filter value, a cursor's `time`, a batch log's `time`) reaches the typed `formatDateTime(\DateTime|string|null)`, which throws a TypeError whose message names the PHP file and line
deviations.reason: Rust: \Exception `Invalid datetime value: <type>`; scalars are coerced to strings as PHP's coercive mode does. The TypeError message quotes PHP source locations; both runtimes reject the input.

deviations.php: A log whose `time` is neither a string, a \DateTime nor null fails `assert()` (or `DateTime::format()`'s type check) with an AssertionError or TypeError naming the PHP file and line
deviations.reason: Rust: \InvalidArgumentException `Log time must be a date string, <type> given`. Logs are arrays of plain values in Rust (no \DateTime objects): a time is a date string, which both runtimes parse as `new \DateTime()` does.

deviations.php: Query values may be \DateTime objects (the adapters format them for the `time` column)
deviations.reason: Rust: Query values are PHP values without \DateTime: pass the date as a string (`Y-m-d H:i:s.v`), which the adapters parse and format to the same literal. The `getBy*()` methods take dates (`Range`). utopia-query's value model has no date object; a string formats to the same ClickHouse literal and the same database value.
